fear_greed.commentary: Sentiment is still in fear at 31, essentially unchanged from the prior close and up slightly from 30 a week ago, even as the Nasdaq jumped 1% on SpaceX's blowout quarter. It remains below last month's 35, so the rally hasn't yet won over cautious investors.

breadth.label: Percent of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
breadth.note: Below 30 bullish, above 70 bearish. Computed by Thaddeus from Yahoo Finance daily closes for 502 of 503 current S&P 500 constituents at the Oct. 21 close (mimics MMFI).

markets.summary: Tech led a broad advance for a third straight S&P 500 gain: the Nasdaq jumped 1.05% to 26,702.86 and the S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7,757.17 as SpaceX's blowout quarter revived the AI trade, lifting chipmakers including NVDA (+2.5%), while the Dow added 0.69% to 52,856.09 and Netflix fell more than 5% on a weak forecast. Breadth improved again to 55.2% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average from 52.0%. Small caps lagged slightly, with the Russell 2000 up 0.27% to 2,781. The 10-year Treasury yield ticked up about 3 basis points to 5.15%. Gold futures edged up 0.2% to $4,150.00 and silver slipped 0.5% to $57.42; both remain below their 40-week averages.

stories.headline: SpaceX jumps after earnings beat as Musk floats a Tesla merger

weather.summary: The nor'easter off the Mid-Atlantic keeps moving out to sea, but onshore winds keep coastal flooding, gales and beach erosion going along parts of the Eastern Seaboard until conditions improve Thursday, and some Northeast and New England spots could see their first frost. A strong low with tropical moisture is pushing into California, the Desert Southwest and the Four Corners, bringing scattered to numerous flash-flood threats through Thursday plus severe storms in central Arizona, shifting to southeast Arizona Thursday. The West turns cool behind a cold front while a ridge keeps the central US above to well above average through the weekend, and the East stays near or below normal.
